items.title: Mona Hinton interviewed by Milt Fillius and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] There’s nobody who plays the sax like Buddy Tate. [INTERVIEWEE] So that’s pretty much why everyone recognized Louis, because that was his signature.

ctx.x: Oh sure, well that’s true. But you know that’s the secret of being, that’s the secret that most musicians should have. Because the minute that I hear Milton playing — we’ll get back to Louis — but I have to tell you this. The minute that I hear something, I can almost tell you that’s Milton Hinton playing, you know why? Because if you notice, see Milton pushed that 16 piece to 17 piece band all those years with Calloway with nothing but a little microphone, you know. So when you hear, you notice it, when you hear…
Well all the great musicians you can say it, just this morning I was standing outside the room and I heard a sound and I said that’s got to be Buddy Tate.
